q: DO Valle Central, Chile's largest region, comprises which four subregions?
exp: Rapel splits further into Cachapoal and Colchagua. Itata, Bío Bío and Malleco are not Central Valley at all — they sit in DO Sur, and Aconcagua is its own region to the north. This matters beyond trivia: the old-vine País and Cinsault revival happens in DO Sur, so a candidate who files Itata under the Central Valley has also lost the geography of Chile's most interesting wines.

q: Argentina's Calchaquí Valleys in Salta are anchored by which town, and what elevation does Bodega Colomé's highest vineyard reach?
accept: cafayate and about 3,111 metres at altura maxima
cafayate colome altura maxima 3111 m
cafayate around 3100 metres elevation
cafayate roughly 1700 m and colome above 3000 m
ans: Cafayate, at roughly 1,700 m; Colomé's Altura Máxima parcel at Payogasta sits at about 3,111 m — among the highest commercial vineyards on earth
exp: Salta is not simply a hotter Mendoza. Latitude 26°S would be unworkable were it not for altitude: the thin, dry air gives punishing daytime sun with nights that fall 20°C, so Torrontés keeps its acidity and Malbec builds skin tannin and colour without flabby sugar. Rainfall is under 200 mm and humidity is negligible, so fungal pressure is close to zero. The trade is fierce UV, wind and hail exposure and yields that make the wines expensive to farm.

q: Under Argentina's INV rules, what minimum ageing must a wine have to be labelled 'Reserva', and what for 'Gran Reserva'?
accept: reserva 12 months red and 6 white gran reserva 24 red and 12 white
12 months reds 6 months whites for reserva twice that for gran reserva
reserva one year for reds gran reserva two years for reds
twelve and six months for reserva twenty four and twelve for gran reserva
ans: Reserva: 12 months for reds, 6 months for whites and rosés. Gran Reserva: 24 months for reds, 12 months for whites and rosés
exp: Argentina legislated these terms (INV Resolution C.32/2011) precisely because they had been decorative, and what the resolution fixes is a stated number of months. Contrast Chile, whose Reserva family hangs on minimum alcohol above the legal floor and on demonstrable oak character rather than any stated ageing period — so 'Reserva' on a Chilean label promises less about elapsed ageing than the same word on an Argentine one. The comparison is a standard trap.

q: Who introduced Malbec to Argentina and in what year, and why does that date matter genetically?
accept: michel pouget in 1853 with pre-phylloxera cuttings
pouget 1853 quinta normal pre phylloxera material
french agronomist pouget in 1853 before phylloxera reached france
ans: The French agronomist Michel Aimé Pouget, brought by Domingo Faustino Sarmiento to found Mendoza's Quinta Normal agricultural school in 1853 — the cuttings pre-date phylloxera, so Argentina preserves French Malbec material largely lost or replanted in Cahors
exp: Argentine Malbec's smaller berries, tighter clusters and darker colour are usually credited to that old material plus 170 years of field selection in a desert without phylloxera pressure — a genetically distinct population, not simply the same grape grown warmer. 17 April, the date Sarmiento moved to found the school, is now Malbec World Day.

q: Viña Leyda's founding in San Antonio required an engineering fix that Casablanca did not. What was it?
accept: a pipeline from the maipo river
an 8 km water pipeline from the maipo
piped irrigation water in from the maipo river
they built a pipeline to bring river water to the plateau
ans: An eight-kilometre pipeline drawing water from the Maipo river — the Leyda plateau had no usable water source, so irrigation had to be piped in before a vine could be planted (1997–98)
exp: Leyda sits some 4 km from the Pacific: cold, windy, cloud-covered mornings and Chile's sharpest Sauvignon Blanc alongside its coolest Pinot Noir and Syrah. The limiting factor was never climate but water, and the pipeline is why a whole subregion exists. It is the clearest illustration that Chilean coastal viticulture is an infrastructure story as much as a terroir one.

q: What makes DO Elqui unusual among Chilean wine valleys, and which red variety made its reputation?
accept: far north high altitude desert valley shared with pisco and syrah
elqui is chile's northern altitude extreme known for syrah
northern desert valley at altitude with pisco competition syrah is the grape
ans: It is the far-northern desert extreme — cloudless skies, extreme UV, vineyards climbing to roughly 2,000 m at Alcohuaz — and it shares its valley floor with Chilean Pisco production; Syrah, cool-fruited and peppery, made its name
exp: Chile's Pisco DO covers the Atacama and Coquimbo regions — Copiapó, Huasco, Elqui, Limarí and Choapa — so Elqui's growers compete for land and irrigation rights with distillers, a constraint no southern valley faces. Cold ocean air funnelling up the narrow valley plus altitude keeps Syrah near 13–14% with real acidity and black-pepper lift, the opposite of the warm-climate Syrah the latitude would suggest.

q: Bandol red must contain what minimum of Mourvèdre?
exp: ≥50% (most run far higher); 18 months minimum in wood.
